articles.title: Latvia to impose national sanctions on Russian oligarchs Usmanov and Fridman after EU compromise
articles.body:
Latvia to impose national sanctions on Russian oligarchs Usmanov and Fridman after EU compromise
Latvia will impose national sanctions on the Russian oligarchs Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman after making concessions and lifting its veto on their removal from the EU sanctions list.
Source: European Pravda, citing a statement by the Latvian government on 22 September
Details: Latvia's Cabinet of Ministers has instructed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to immediately draw up a proposal, legal justification and the necessary draft legislation to enable Latvia to impose national sanctions on Usmanov and Fridman.
Quote: "Latvia will continue to use all legal instruments at its disposal to prevent the unfreezing of these individuals' funds and economic resources in Latvia."
More details: The Cabinet of Ministers also said that at a closed meeting on 22 September, it had agreed on Latvia's position on extending EU sanctions against Russia. The deal ensured that personal sanctions against more than 2,600 Russian supporters of the war and related individuals and entities would be extended for the next three years. Up until now, the decision has had to be taken every six months.
During the procedure for the adoption of the decision by the Council of the EU, however, Latvia's representative will abstain from voting in order to maintain and publicly express Latvia's political opposition to the lifting of EU sanctions on the two oligarchs.
"Throughout the negotiations with the leaders of EU member states, Latvia opposed the removal of politically motivated individuals from the individual sanctions list and was the only EU member state to maintain this position until the very end. It was the morally right position, and our allies in Ukraine appreciated it," Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs said.
He added that "this was not a choice between a good and a bad decision, but between a bad one and a much worse one – a choice between changing the status of two individuals and the future of the entire sanctions regime".
Quote from Kulbergs: "By deciding to continue imposing sanctions on these individuals, we have achieved an outcome that is more beneficial for Latvia, Ukraine and Europe in the long term."
Background:
- Amid the announcement of Riga's decision, it was reported that French President Emmanuel Macron has agreed to begin talks with Latvia on joining France's nuclear deterrence initiative, and that France has committed to strengthening its military presence in Latvia.
- European Pravda sources in French diplomatic circles explained why Paris wanted to lift sanctions on Usmanov. It later emerged that France planned to "exchange" Usmanov's delisting for the release of several French citizens who are currently in prison in Azerbaijan.

articles.title: Netanyahu to cut short NYC trip amid protests, Mamdani threat
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Netanyahu to cut short NYC visit amid protests, Mamdani arrest threat
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has dramatically shortened his visit to New York for the UN General Assembly, amid planned protests, heightened security and tensions with Mayor Zohran Mamdani over the International Criminal Court warrant for his arrest.
Netanyahu is expected to arrive in the US on Thursday morning, address the General Assembly at 2pm New York time and leave for Israel later that evening, according to Israeli media reports.
The Israeli leader is not expected to spend a single night in the US, cutting what had initially been planned as a longer visit to just several hours. He has also cancelled a planned stop in Texas to meet billionaire Elon Musk and will not take Israeli journalists aboard his official "Wing of Zion" aircraft.
Israeli media cited planned protests and security concerns among the reasons for the unusually brief visit.
According to Ynet, Netanyahu's plane is expected to avoid New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport and instead land in neighbouring New Jersey.
The outlet linked the arrangements partly to tensions with Mamdani, who has repeatedly called for Netanyahu to face arrest over the ICC warrant.
Other Israeli reporting, however, has attributed the decision to avoid JFK to logistical and security considerations surrounding Netanyahu's aircraft.
Mamdani has been an outspoken critic of Netanyahu and previously pledged to have the Israeli leader arrested if he travelled to New York, citing the ICC warrant issued against him in November 2024.
The mayor acknowledged in July, however, that New York City does not independently possess the legal authority to enforce the warrant.
"It is clear that we do not have the independent legal authority to enforce this warrant," Mamdani said at the time, while calling on the US federal government to join the ICC and execute it.
He has nevertheless maintained that Netanyahu is not welcome in New York and has continued to describe him as a war criminal over Israel's actions in Gaza.
The ICC issued arrest warrants for Netanyahu and former Israeli defence minister Yoav Gallant in November 2024, saying there were reasonable grounds to believe they bore criminal responsibility for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during Israel's war on Gaza.
Israel rejects the allegations and does not recognise the court's jurisdiction. The US is also not a member of the ICC.
US President Donald Trump said in July that Netanyahu would not be arrested in the United States.
Heavy security and protests expected
Netanyahu is expected to receive unusually heavy security protection during his brief stay, with US Secret Service involvement in preparations for the visit reportedly greater than usual.
Large demonstrations are also expected in New York during his visit.
Haaretz reported that Netanyahu is preparing for a hostile reception both on the streets and inside the General Assembly, where Israeli officials anticipate that ambassadors and other delegates could walk out or stage protests during his speech.
A mass walkout took place when Netanyahu addressed the General Assembly last year.
Mamdani has said he does not plan to participate in protests against Netanyahu during the visit and has been coordinating with the New York Police Department over security surrounding UNGA.
Netanyahu is not expected to meet Trump during the trip, and a meeting with Secretary of State Marco Rubio has also not been confirmed.
His address comes around a month before Israel's general election, with Israeli media reporting that the speech is expected to focus heavily on Iran while also being aimed at a domestic Israeli audience.
Israeli officials are meanwhile hoping protests inside the General Assembly will be smaller than last year, amid international attention on the war with Iran and Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
Israel continues to occupy most of the Gaza Strip and carry out deadly air strikes, shelling and gunfire despite the October 2025 ceasefire.
More than 73,900 Palestinians have been killed and nearly 175,000 wounded since October 2023, including around 1,400 killed since the ceasefire took effect.
Most of Gaza's roughly 2.1 million people remain displaced, while Israeli restrictions continue to impede the entry of critical humanitarian and reconstruction supplies.

articles.title: Ukraine hits Russian oil refineries in Samara and Ufa
articles.body:
Ukraine hits Russian oil refineries in Samara and Ufa
Units from the Ukrainian defence forces struck two key oil refining facilities in Russia on the night of 21-22 September.
Sources: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine; Special Operations Forces (SOF)
Details: The Kuibyshev oil refinery in Samara was struck.
The Special Operations Forces said the attack was carried out by Special Operations Forces' Deep Strike units jointly with the Unmanned Systems Forces and Defence Intelligence of Ukraine. Several drones reached their targets, causing a large-scale fire at the facility.
The Kuibyshev oil refinery is one of the largest oil refining facilities in Russia's Samara group and is part of the Rosneft structure. It has a refining capacity of around 7 million tonnes of oil per year. The refinery produces petrol, diesel fuel, fuel oil and more than 30 other petroleum products.
The Bashneft-Ufaneftekhim oil refinery in Ufa, Republic of Bashkortostan, Russia, was also struck, with a fire reported on the premises.
Bashneft-Ufaneftekhim has a refining capacity of around 7.5 million tonnes of oil per year. The facility carries out deep oil refining and produces petrol, diesel and boiler fuel, liquefied gases, sulphur and other petroleum products.
Products from both refineries are used to meet the needs of the Russian military.

articles.title: New group of US troops 'on its way' to Lithuania, says the Lithuanian president
articles.body:
Trump deploys fresh US troops to Lithuania, says country’s president, amid cuts in Europe
- A new rotation of US troops is already on its way to Lithuania, according to President Gitanas Nauseda.
- Nauseda thanked President Donald Trump and the US administration, calling the presence vital for Lithuania and regional security.
- Despite US troop withdrawals from Europe, Lithuania emphasises the US military presence as key for deterrence and collective defence.
AI generated
VILNIUS - The United States has confirmed that it is sending a new rotation of troops to Lithuania, the Baltic NATO country said on Sept 22, ending a period of uncertainty over whether the US military would replace forces that returned home this summer.
The US is withdrawing thousands of troops from bases in Europe, and Lithuania, which shares borders with Russia and Belarus, said in June it had learned that the US was reviewing its future military presence in the country.
“I have just received confirmation that the new rotation of US troops is already on its way to Lithuania,” President Gitanas Nauseda wrote in a post on social media X.
Nauseda thanked President Donald Trump and the US administration, adding that this was important for Lithuania and for the security of the region.
“The US military presence in Lithuania is an indispensable part of our deterrence and collective defence,” Nauseda said.
He did not say how many service members the next rotation would contain.
Since 2019, the US has usually deployed an armoured battalion of about 1,000 troops in the country.
Lithuania‘s Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said the US deployment was “returning to large numbers”, but did not provide details.
“Lithuania is indeed a strong and reliable partner, and today we received proof of that,” Budrys said in a statement.
The US embassy in Vilnius did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside of regular business hours. REUTERS

articles.title: Ukrainian troops killed 40 occupiers and wounded another 14 in the Pokrovsk direction — General Staff
articles.body:
Ukrainian troops killed 40 occupiers and wounded another 14 in the Pokrovsk direction — General Staff
Kyiv • UNN
The General Staff reported 197 combat engagements, 50 airstrikes and more than 6,000 enemy kamikaze drones. In the Pokrovsk direction, 40 occupiers were killed.
Overall, since the beginning of this day, 197 combat engagements have taken place at the front. In the Pokrovsk direction, Ukrainian troops repelled 23 attacks and also eliminated 40 occupiers, with another 14 wounded, UNN reports, citing a General Staff briefing.
The enemy launched 50 airstrikes and dropped 168 guided aerial bombs. In addition, it deployed 6,137 kamikaze drones for strikes and carried out 1,930 shelling attacks on settlements and the positions of our troops
No offensive activity by the enemy was recorded in the North Slobozhanskyi and Kursk directions.
During the day, in the South Slobozhanskyi direction, the enemy stormed the positions of our units seven times near Kozacha Lopan, Lyman, Symynivka, Rybальchyne and Zarubynka; two more combat engagements are still ongoing.
In the Kupiansk direction, the Defense Forces repelled one enemy assault near Kivsharivka.
In the Lyman direction, our defenders successfully repelled two attempts by the invaders to advance near Shyikivka, Novoselivka and Derylove; one more combat engagement is ongoing.
In the Sloviansk direction, the Defense Forces stopped three attempts by the invaders to advance near Ozerne, Mykolaivka and Rai-Oleksandrivka.
One enemy assault was recorded in the Kramatorsk direction near Fedorivka Druha.
In the Kostiantynivka direction, the Defense Forces repelled 14 enemy assaults near Kostiantynivka, Novoselivka, Illinivka, Dovha Balka, Rozkishne and Novopavlivka; one more combat engagement is ongoing.
A total of 23 attacks were repelled in the Pokrovsk direction. The occupiers attempted to advance near the settlements of Toretskе, Sofiivka, Dobropillia, Novyi Donbas, Vilne, Bilytske, Hannivka, Krasnopodillia, Vodianske, Dorozhnіe, Vasylivka, Myrne, Serhiivka and Novopavlivka. Three combat engagements are ongoing.
According to preliminary estimates, 40 occupiers were eliminated here today and 14 wounded; two vehicles, two pieces of special equipment, one unmanned aerial vehicle command post and 55 enemy shelters were destroyed. Two vehicles, six artillery systems, two pieces of special equipment, seven unmanned aerial vehicle command posts and 178 enemy shelters were damaged. A total of 103 unmanned aerial vehicles of various types were destroyed or suppressed.
In the Oleksandrivka direction, the occupiers took no active action.
Ten occupier attacks were recorded in the Huliaipole direction near the settlements of Rizdvianka, Ternuvate and Kopani.
In the Orikhiv direction, our defenders repelled two enemy attacks near Pavlivka.
There were no enemy assault operations in the Prydniprovske direction.
There were no significant changes in the situation in the other directions, the General Staff concluded.

articles.title: Poland scrambles air force over threat of Russian drones
articles.body:
Poland scrambles air force over threat of Russian drones
In response to Russia’s airstrikes on Ukrainian territory, military aircraft have been deployed in Polish airspace, according to a statement by the Operational Command of the Polish Armed Forces on X, as reported by Ukrinform.
In accordance with established procedures, the Operational Command of the Armed Forces, through the Air Operations Center—Air Component Command, has activated the necessary forces and resources at its disposal. Ground-based air defense systems and radar reconnaissance have been brought to a state of readiness.
These measures are preventive in nature and aimed at securing and defending airspace, particularly in areas adjacent to regions posing a threat, the publication adds.
As reported by Ukrinform, Poland is strengthening civil defense measures along its eastern border by installing more than 1,000 automated sirens.

articles.title: Russia encircles key Ukrainian defense hub – MOD
articles.body:
Russia encircles key Ukrainian defense hub – MOD
Russian forces have completed the encirclement of Dobropolye, a major Ukrainian defensive hub in Russia’s Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR), the Defense Ministry in Moscow has announced.
In a statement on Tuesday, the ministry said that units from Russia’s ‘Center’ group had surrounded the town and were now moving toward the settlement of Aleksandrovka.
The advance is part of a broader Russian push toward the Slavyansk-Kramatorsk agglomeration, a string of cities in the northwest of DPR and the last heavily fortified Ukrainian stronghold in the region.
The agglomeration has remained under Kiev’s control for over a decade since the early stage of the conflict in then-Ukrainian Donbass, prompted by the 2014 Maidan coup.
Capturing Dobropolye could facilitate a Russian advance toward the agglomeration from the southwest while threatening Ukrainian supply and reinforcement routes.
Aleksandrovka is significant in this respect, as Russian military sources have described the western route running through the settlement as one of the last remaining supply arteries for Ukrainian forces in the area.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said in June that Ukraine had spent almost a decade constructing a strategic defensive line encompassing the Slavyansk-Kramatorsk area and extending southwest toward Dobropolye. The cities were transformed into a single fortified zone by a vast system of reinforced trenches, bunkers, and tunnels.
He added that Russian troops had breached a three-tier line of fortifications on the approaches to Dobropolye and claimed that Kiev had no comparable prepared defenses immediately to its north, forcing Ukrainian troops to hastily construct local strongpoints.
The Russian Defense Ministry also said that troops from Ukraine’s 4th and 15th National Guard brigades and the 425th Separate Assault Regiment, known as “Skala” or “Skelya,” were among those trapped in the town. “Operations are underway to eliminate” the surrounded Ukrainian forces, it added.
“Skala” came under scrutiny earlier this year after Ukrainian media reported torture and abuse at its training facilities, as well as 25 non-combat deaths among recruits. Ukrainian authorities subsequently opened an investigation and suspended the regiment’s commander.
As Russian forces continue to advance in Donbass, Moscow has accused Kiev of intensifying attacks on civilian targets, repeatedly describing such strikes as acts of terrorism. The Defense Ministry has warned that the targeting of civilian facilities would be met by intensified precision strikes on military targets in Kiev.
On Tuesday, a major Ukrainian drone raid on the Samara Region left one person dead and four injured, according to Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev. He said private homes and vehicles were also damaged.

Kang Jun-young is a professor at the Graduate School of International and Area Studies, Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, and chairman of the Northeast Asia Future Cooperation Forum. 
The September 24 summit between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump is no ordinary engagement. Their May summit took place in Beijing and largely centred on economic issues. This one will be on Trump’s home turf and is expected to put strategic questions on the table. Will the Korean peninsula and North Korea’s nuclear programme again be pushed to the margins?
In Beijing, both sides focused on their immediate national interests, such as trade, semiconductors, rare earths and Taiwan. The issue of the peninsula’s security threat never appeared on the agenda.

articles.title: France to srengthen Ukraine’s air defense with radars, interceptor missiles — Macron
articles.body:
France to srengthen Ukraine’s air defense with radars, interceptor missiles — Macron
Ukrinform reports this, citing French President Emmanuel Macron’s post on X, following a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in New York.
“We are strengthening Ukraine’s air defense by signing a contract for the supply of radars, as well as providing interceptors,” Macron said.
The French president did not specify the number or types of weapons involved or the timeline for their delivery.
During an in-depth discussion with Zelensky, the two leaders also discussed threats to Ukraine’s energy system ahead of winter. Macron said.
“Russian strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure threaten to leave millions of families without heating and electricity. France will stand with Ukraine to help it get through the winter. The G7 energy format will also be mobilized in support of Ukraine,” the French president stressed.
The French President said he had discussed support for Ukraine with Donald Trump, including the prospects for an energy ceasefire and the introduction of a moratorium on strikes in the Black Sea.
“This will be one of the issues on the agenda of negotiations that must resume and lead to a just and lasting peace,” he concluded.
As previously reported by Ukrinform, Zelensky, following his meeting with Macron, said they had discussed security issues and a winter support package for Ukraine. work was underway on the possibility of producing such air defense systems and missiles for them in Ukraine, as well as on a joint anti-ballistic program, “Freya,” with partners, Zelensky said.
Photo: @EmmanuelMacron

articles.title: US leaves Middle Eastern ally hanging (VIDEO)
articles.body:
US leaves Middle Eastern ally hanging (VIDEO)
The US seems to be in no rush to bail out Saudi Arabia while renewed hostilities with Yemen’s Houthis are ongoing, RT’s Steve Sweeney reports from Beirut. The New York Times claimed over the weekend that US President Donald Trump had called off air strikes on the Shiite militant group at the last minute.
The conflict between Riyadh and the Houthis reignited in mid-July, with the armed group recently conducting strikes on several “sensitive sites” across Saudi Arabia, including the main airport in the capital. Earlier this month, the organization, officially known as Ansarullah, established control over Yemen’s Red Sea coast, taking positions around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Saudi Arabia has increasingly relied on the key waterway for its oil exports since navigation through another strategically important maritime chokepoint, the Strait of Hormuz, was reduced to a trickle amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
After a phone call from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Thursday, Trump initially seemed to acquiesce to his request for help in deterring the Houthis’ advances in Yemen, the NYT cited anonymous US officials as saying. However, on Sunday, as the US military was supposedly all set to bomb selected targets in Yemen, the American president reversed his decision, the publication reported.
The US carried out weeks of strikes on the Houthis’ positions last year, with the stated goal of restoring freedom of navigation in the Red Sea as well as stopping attacks on commercial vessels and American warships there.
Less than two months into the campaign, Trump announced a cease-fire, saying that Ansarullah had promised not to attack US ships. According to the NYT, the Houthis have kept their word, with Trump’s advisers now “deeply skeptical” about reengaging the Shiite group militarily once again, especially given reported ammunition shortages incurred as a result of the conflict with Iran.
Saudi Arabia’s regional allies Türkiye and Pakistan apparently have little appetite to join the fray either, despite being bound by the recently sealed Mecca defense pact, and are calling for a diplomatic solution instead.
Meanwhile, the Houthis have explicitly warned other countries against getting involved in their conflict with the Saudis. Speaking to AP on Sunday, the group’s spokesperson, Mohamed al-Bukhaiti, said that Ansarullah was “not targeting the United States, or any other nation, in the strait, with the sole exception of the Saudi enemy.” At the same time, he stressed that the Houthis were prepared to fight on multiple fronts, if necessary.
